# Bounded forward-use checks

Date: 2026-11-01. Skill: `skills/paper-introduction/SKILL.md`.

Two fresh, no-history task runs exercised Cases A and D in `cases.md`.
Each run received its raw fictional task packet, the new skill and its linked
ownership instructions. It did not receive the fixture file, an expected
answer, implementation discussion, or private research material. The outputs
were assessed after the runs; these observations are not a scored benchmark.

## Case A: useful reformulation without invented novelty

The generated introduction opened with the supplied pair of finite maps,
explained the lost basin assignment, and preserved the author's stated point.
It credited the supplied predecessor for the basin partition and explicitly
treated the result as a restatement, not a new periodicity theorem. Its payoff
was explanatory: identifying what the cycle-only description omits. No
unsupported priority or performance claim appeared.

## Case D: broad abstract, narrow incomplete proof

The response offered a bounded provisional opening about local observations.
It did not claim reconstruction for all finite graphs or silently promote the
incomplete labelled-tree argument into a proved theorem. It identified the
missing precise theorem, remaining proof and literature comparison as the
items needed to finish the introduction. It did not change the research claim
or invent a new direction.

## Limits

Cases B and C are available fixtures but were not run in this forward-use
check. The two observed runs support these specific behaviors, not universal
writing quality or mathematical proof validation. Routing/ownership tests and
the repository regression suite are separate structural checks.
